[Thinking]
**Creating JS code**

I'm focusing on crafting a JavaScript function that effectively removes the pattern "(age x)" from a given string. First, I need to utilize a regular expression to identify the pattern I want to eliminate. Then, I'll test the function with various strings to ensure its reliability. I'll make sure it's well-commented so that others can understand its functionality easily. Let's get going on implementing this code and ensure it works as intended!
[/Thinking]

You can use a regular expression to remove the `(age X)` part, where `X` can be any number:

```javascript
const text = "july 7 1994 (age 7) London, UK (1994-07-07)";

const result = text.replace(/\s*\(age \d+\)/, "");

console.log(result);
// "july 7 1994 London, UK (1994-07-07)"
```

### If you want it to remove any number:
- `\d+` matches one or more digits
- `\s*` removes any extra spaces before `(age X)`

### If you want to remove all occurrences in the string:
```javascript
const result = text.replace(/\s*\(age \d+\)/g, "");
```

If you want, I can also show a version that removes `(age X)` even if there are extra spaces like `( age 7 )`.
